items.statement: The username and password fields each carry an accessible name from a label element tied to them by id, or from aria-labelledby; placeholder text is not counted as a name.
items.why: A field without a name is announced as an unlabelled edit box, and a placeholder vanishes as soon as typing starts.

verify.how: For each of the two inputs, quote the label (or aria-labelledby target) whose for/id pairing names it. An input whose only text is a placeholder answers fail.

naWhen: the form has no text input (single sign-on button only)

items.statement: The identifier input declares autocomplete="username" (or "email") and the password input autocomplete="current-password".
items.why: Password managers fill and save credentials only when the purpose of each field is declared.

verify.how: The harness searches the changed files for a current-password autocomplete value; absent is a fail.

items.statement: No handler on the password field cancels paste, copy or drop events.
items.why: Blocking paste stops people from using a password manager and pushes them to short, memorable passwords.

verify.how: The harness searches the changed files for a paste handler that calls preventDefault; present is a fail.

items.statement: The inputs are inside a form element whose submission is handled by its submit event, with a button of type submit, so Enter submits from either field.
items.why: A click handler on a div or a button outside a form cannot be reached by the Enter key or by a password manager's autofill-and-submit.

verify.how: Quote the form element with its onSubmit (or submit listener) and the submit button. A click handler on a non-button element answers fail.

items.statement: An unknown account and a wrong password produce the same message, the same status code and the same page state.
items.why: Different answers tell anyone with the form which accounts exist.

verify.how: A test that signs in once with an unknown identifier and once with a known identifier and a wrong password, and asserts both responses are identical.
verify.check: npm test -- --testNamePattern 'same failure for unknown account and wrong password'

items.statement: A failed sign-in puts its message in a live region (role=alert or aria-live) and marks the offending field aria-invalid with aria-describedby pointing at the message.
items.why: An error shown only as red text near the field is never read out to a screen reader user.

verify.how: Quote the element that renders the failure message with its role or aria-live, and the input's aria-invalid and aria-describedby. Either missing answers fail.

items.statement: While the sign-in request is pending the submit control is disabled or ignored, and it is enabled again when the request fails.
items.why: Two requests for one sign-in can trip lockouts, and a button left disabled after an error leaves the person stuck.

verify.how: Quote where the pending flag is set before the request, and where it is cleared on the failure path (a finally block or the catch). A flag cleared only on success answers fail.

items.statement: The form offers a link or button to reset a forgotten password, reachable by keyboard.
items.why: Without it a person who forgot the password has no way forward from this screen.

verify.how: Quote the anchor or button and its destination or handler. An element reachable only by mouse (a span with onClick) answers fail.

naWhen: the product has no passwords (magic links or single sign-on only)

items.statement: The credentials are sent with POST in the request body, never in a query string, and no logging or analytics call on the sign-in path receives the password.
items.why: Query strings and logs are stored and copied far from the sign-in path, and a password there is a leak.

verify.how: Quote the request call showing its method and body. Search the sign-in handler for console, logger and analytics calls and quote any that receive form values; one that receives the password answers fail.

items.statement: No style removes the focus outline from the form's inputs, links or buttons without a visible replacement in the same rule.
items.why: Keyboard users lose track of where they are when focus is invisible.

verify.how: Search the form's styles for outline: none or outline: 0. For each match quote the replacement focus style beside it, or answer fail; with no match, answer pass and quote the style file you searched.

items.statement: After a failed attempt the identifier keeps its value and focus moves to the message or to the first invalid field.
items.why: Retyping the identifier and hunting for the error are what make people give up after a failed sign-in.

verify.how: A browser test that submits a wrong password, then asserts the identifier field still holds its value and document.activeElement is the error region or the first invalid input.

items.statement: At a 320 CSS pixel wide viewport and at 200% zoom the whole form is usable without scrolling sideways, and its text meets the contrast minimum.
items.why: The sign-in screen is the one screen every user has to get through, on every device.

verify.how: Open the page in a browser at 320 pixels wide and again at 200% zoom; check that nothing is cut off or needs sideways scrolling, and check label and error text with a contrast checker.
